name: Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome Due to Defects in Endplate Development and Maintenance

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with onset in infancy or early childhood
Electrophysiological evidence of impaired neuromuscular transmission (e.g., decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in endplate development and maintenance (e.g., COLQ, LAMB2, AGRN)
Histopathological evidence of endplate structural abnormalities
Clinical improvement with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or other CMS-specific therapies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with electrophysiological evidence of neuromuscular transmission defect plus identification of pathogenic variants in relevant genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is critical due to phenotypic overlap with other neuromuscular disorders.

searchTerms: muscle weakness that worsens with use
drooping eyelid that worsens with tiredness

common.symptomName: Dysphagia due to bulbar muscle involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing due to throat muscle weakness
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness
drooping eyelid with complete eye muscle paralysis
ptosis combined with total eye movement loss
eyelid droop and frozen eye muscles

laboratory: Electromyography showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
imaging: Muscle MRI may show selective muscle involvement
Chest imaging may reveal atelectasis or aspiration pneumonia secondary to bulbar weakness
genetic: Pathogenic variants in COLQ, LAMB2, AGRN, or related genes affecting endplate development and maintenance
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating abnormal neuromuscular junction morphology
Positive response to acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or 3,4-diaminopyridine in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Later onset compared to congenital forms
Genetic mutations affecting presynaptic or synaptic proteins rather than endplate structure

redFlags: Severe bulbar weakness causing aspiration risk
Lack of response to standard acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
references: Engel AG, Shen XM, Selcen D, Sine SM. Congenital myasthenic syndromes: pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment. Lancet Neurol. 2015;14(4):420-434.
Orphanet: Congenital myasthenic syndrome due to defects in endplate development and maintenance (ORPHA:716825)
